speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what enforcement actions can the Ministry take against errant employers found to have practised workplace discrimination especially on grounds of age and race.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We urge employee who experience any workplace discrimination to approach MOM or TAFEP for assistance.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can the Ministry actually do more in the area of greater awareness of fair employment best practises among employers, such as adopting similar like BizSafe framework, where senior executives of firms undergo structured training.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And further to that, making it a requirement to attend such training first before one can participate in Government tenders, so that firms are clearly motivated to deepen knowledge in this particular area of fair best practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we will take the Member's suggestions and study how we can better do this at workplaces by actively correcting stereotypes and changing employers' mindsets through more promotional efforts.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With regard to the Senior Minister of State's reply on workplace discrimination, can the Minister consider naming these errant employers who are found to have practised workplace discrimination, with the intent that by naming them, both the company and the employees in the company will be motivated to adopt fair employment practices as soon as possible?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can the Ministry also consider that given that SMEs account for more than two-thirds of employment in Singapore, can such training for SMEs before they can recruit or hire individuals be made compulsory?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Firms that are on this watch list, technically, they have not flouted any rules yet but, perhaps, some of their practices may be veering on the grey margins.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is through putting them on the watch list that we use it as a way to engage the firms and signal to them that their practices have to be improved.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In this instance, such engagement is also an educational effort for companies or firms that may not be aware, upfront, of the nuancing of the guidelines on fair employment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think we want to take a very educational approach because not every firm that may on prima facie seems to have infringed on some of the regulations, could be doing it in a very deliberate way.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Sometimes, through these efforts, firms do change their practices for the better.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It may then have the negative consequence of impeding some of the business functions that these firms have as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We would want to probably go on the more educational approach.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: One important observation, as the Senior Minister of State rightly pointed out, education is important.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: But the HR community as well as the employment agents and agency community are two communities which, we feel very strongly, need to be better educated, be given knowledge and awareness of some of these advisories, guidelines, including legislation, particularly, as many of them are from multinational companies and across the globe.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: So, can I suggest to the Senior Minister of State to pay particular attention to these two groups?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we will increase our engagement with these intermediaries such as HR practitioners.
